text: When AEB is enabled and vehicle speed is 10–50 km/h, the system shall monitor forward pedestrian collision risk.
A pedestrian track sustained for at least 200 ms shall be provided to the Risk Assessor.
If predicted vehicle path intersects a pedestrian and TTC <= 1.5 s, the system shall generate a warning request.
If TTC <= 1.0 s and collision path is maintained, generate an automatic brake request within 150 ms.
During automatic braking, maintain the brake request until collision risk is cleared.
When driver override is detected, the AEB Supervisor shall receive the override state.
The system shall not generate an automatic brake request for a pedestrian outside the predicted vehicle path.
If a mandatory sensor input is invalid, automatic braking shall be inhibited and a Degraded state shall be output.
Each AEB decision record shall include timestamp, requirement ID, input state, and trigger reason.
Each executed test shall store scenario conditions, expected result, actual result, and Pass/Fail status.
The system shall brake sufficiently quickly when collision risk is high.
An AI-generated test shall not be promoted to Approved without Human Review.
